We need to cluster equivalent facts. Let's list each candidate's proposition.

0: Luke's gospel describes interaction between Jesus and women among the crowd of mourners. qualifier point in time Luke 23:28-31.

1: Jesus said (long quote) (the whole passage) with point in time Luke 23:28-31.

2: women among the crowd of mourners follow Jesus. No qualifiers.

3: Jesus addressed Daughters of Jerusalem. No qualifiers.

4: Luke's gospel describes interaction between Jesus and the women among the crowd of mourners. No qualifiers. (subject_type religious text vs written work but same entity.)

5: Jesus interacted with women among the crowd of mourners, qualifier source Luke's gospel.

6: Jesus addressed Daughters of Jerusalem. (same as 3)

7: Jesus said "Do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children" with addressee Daughters of Jerusalem.

8: Jesus prophesied "Days are coming when they will say 'Blessed are the barren...'" addressee Daughters of Jerusalem.

9: Crucifixion of Jesus instance of event. (unique)

10: Luke's gospel describes interaction between Jesus and women among the crowd of mourners. (same as 0/4 but no qualifier)

11: Jesus said "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children" (no addressee qualifier). Slightly shorter than 7 (no addressee). But 7 includes addressee Daughters of Jerusalem. Are they equivalent? 7 says subject Jesus said that phrase, addressee Daughters of Jerusalem. 11 says same phrase but no explicit addressee; but the phrase itself includes "Daughters of Jerusalem," so the addressee is implicit. Does that count as same complete proposition? The proposition includes the content of the statement. The addressee qualifier is redundant because the statement addresses them. The core proposition: Jesus said that phrase. Both convey same. The qualifier addressee may be considered redundant, not adding substantive info. According to rules, qualifier that is redundant can be considered equivalent. So 7 and 11 likely equivalent.

12: Jesus said "the days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren...'" (no addressee). 8 says prophesied same with addressee Daughters of Jerusalem. Also relation differs: 8 uses relation "prophesied", 12 uses "said". Are they equivalent? The paragraph: Jesus says "For behold, the days are coming when they will say..." That's a statement of prophecy. Relation "said" vs "prophesied". Are they synonymous? Possibly "prophesied" is a more specific type of saying. The rule: synonyms allowed if same meaning. "said" is generic; "prophesied" is more specific but still a kind of saying. However the complete proposition includes relation type. If one says "Jesus said X" and another "Jesus prophesied X", are they the same complete proposition? Might be considered equivalent because the content is that he said a prophecy. But the relation difference could be considered a substantive difference? The rule says synonyms allowed. "prophesied" could be considered a synonym of "said" in this context? Might be okay. However also 8 includes addressee qualifier Daughters of Jerusalem, while 12 lacks. The phrase includes "the days are coming..." but not address. The addressee may be implicit (the audience). In the paragraph, Jesus is speaking to the women (Daughters of Jerusalem). So addressee is implied. The qualifier may be redundant. So 8 and 12 could be equivalent.

13: Jesus said "they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us'". Unique.

14: Jesus said "if they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?" Unique.

15: women among the crowd of mourners follow Jesus (same as 2). So 2 and 15 are duplicates.

Now group candidates about Luke's gospel describing interaction.

0,4,10 are same description but 0 has qualifier point in time; 4 and 10 have none. The qualifier adds point in time (Luke 23:28-31). Is that a substantive restriction? The description "describes interaction" is about the content; adding a point in time qualifier indicates that the description occurs at that passage. Does that change the proposition? The core proposition: Luke's gospel describes interaction between Jesus and women among the crowd of mourners. Adding a qualifier "point in time Luke 23:28-31" adds extra info about where in the gospel. That is an additional restriction, not present in others. According to rules, extra qualifier makes it not equivalent because one has extra restriction. So 0 is not equivalent to 4/10. 4 and 10 are identical (subject_type difference but same entity). So group: 4 and 10 together.

Now candidate 5: Jesus interacted with women among the crowd of mourners, source Luke's gospel. This is similar to 0/4/10 but with relation "interacted with" vs "describes interaction". Also includes source qualifier. The core proposition: Jesus interacted with women among the crowd of mourners. That's a claim about event, not about description. The others are about Luke's gospel describing it. So not equivalent.

Now 1: Jesus said the whole long quote (including all parts). This is a composite statement containing multiple sentences. Others break into parts. 1 includes entire passage. 7,11,8,12,13,14 each are fragments. Are they equivalent? No, because 1 includes all those statements together. So not equivalent.

Now 3 and 6: both "Jesus addressed Daughters of Jerusalem". identical. So group 3,6.

Now 7 and 11: as discussed, likely equivalent. Also maybe 7 includes addressee qualifier; 11 lacks. Should be equivalent.

Now 8 and 12: maybe equivalent. Also 8 uses relation "prophesied". Might be considered synonym. I'd treat as equivalent.

Now 2 and 15: group.

Now 0 stands alone.

Now 5 stands alone.

Now 9 stands alone.

Now 13 stands alone.

Now 14 stands alone.

Now check any other duplicates: maybe 0 vs 5? 0 is about Luke's gospel describing interaction; 5 is about Jesus interacting (source Luke's gospel). Not same.

Now produce groups list with members IDs and representative chosen as a clear member.

Let's decide representatives:

Group A: [4,10] choose 4 (has subject_type religious text vs written work; both fine but 4 maybe clearer). Representative 4.

Group B: [3,6] choose 3.

Group C: [7,11] choose 7 (has addressee qualifier but clear).

Group D: [8,12] choose 8 (prophesied maybe more specific but okay). Could also choose 12. Choose 8.

Group E: [2,15] choose 2.

payload.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
payload.paragraph_text: Luke's gospel also describes an interaction between Jesus and the women among the crowd of mourners following him, quoting Jesus as saying "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children. For behold, the days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren and the wombs that never bore and the breasts that never nursed!' Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us.' For if they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?"[Lk. 23:28-31]
